title: Lock/sleep: fail-closed, clamshell, auth UI, lid focus, logind
head: 01dbad100b65
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Permanent EOF in dbus-monitor makes the new sleep-monitor loop spin through delay-inhibitor acquisitions without the unit failing
leads.consequence: A dbus-monitor startup failure or closed event stream returns success from the --inhibited and --wait-resume children; when PreparingForSleep reads false, the parent immediately starts another systemd-inhibit and monitor instead of letting systemd RestartSec back off. The unit remains active and repeatedly forks/logs without keeping a stable sleep-event subscriber. A later suspend can run without a lock. Gate EOF/nonzero and back off or exit nonzero so the service supervisor can retry.
leads.triage: confirmed by Opus follow-up-1 (mocked runs); published as N1

leads.summary: The new shared lid/undock helper retains physical-connector gating even when an external connector is not a usable Hyprland display
leads.consequence: If the lid is closed with a connected DRM external connector that Hyprland does not expose, the helper sees hardware external and skips locking both on lid close and after undocking. Open PR #10713 fixes the original lid-close path by using the active-display predicate but cannot repair this PR's new helper without an explicit change. Its lid-close hunk conflicts on three-way merge. Adapt the shared helper and both call sites, including its Touch-Bar-style scenario, rather than resolving only the old lid-close hunk.
leads.triage: dropped: narrow Touch Bar hardware case resting on open #10713's premise; pre-existing PR logic, low value for this follow-up

leads.summary: Open #9523 would reintroduce the cross-surface lockView id reference removed by this revision if merged without adapting its secure-state hook
leads.consequence: #9523 adds lockView.forcePasswordFocus() in the secure-state handler; current Service removes id: lockView from WlSessionLockSurface and uses root.passwordFocusRequest instead. The three-way merge conflicts at this handler (not silently clean). A reconciliation preserving the old call would throw ReferenceError when the session secures and lose the focus fix. Update #9523's hook to root.forceLockPasswordFocus() and its assertion, retaining this PR's timer cleanup. Treat as an integration conflict, not an already broken current-head path.
leads.triage: verified factually and dropped: #9523 at 5a026f6 already reads lockView from Service scope while id is declared inside WlSessionLockSurface (its own lines 241/270), so the defect is #9523's own, not a conflict created by this PR

leads.summary: With open #9429's synchronous system-lock verification, the new lid/undock helper stalls display reconciliation for the full 10-second lock timeout
leads.consequence: When the lid is closed with no available real display, this revision holds lockRequested pending until a screen exists, but calls omarchy-system-lock synchronously before omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell can re-enable the internal panel. #9429 makes that lock command wait up to 10 seconds for secure, then emit a critical failure notification. Clamshell reconciliation is delayed until the timeout, contrary to the other PR's premise that this path is not racing suspend. Preserve the prompt lock request but move or bound the secure-state wait so display recovery is not held behind it.
leads.triage: confirmed by Opus follow-up-1 (mocked runs) and coordinator read of #9429 patch; published as N2

leads.summary: The revised no-real-screen timeout test passes even if that branch drops lockRequested
leads.consequence: The new regex checks only that the if and timer restart appear somewhere later, not that lockRequested remains set. A plausible regression reintroducing prior F2 in this branch passes; assert the actual branch state for headless timeout (or execute a small extracted state transition) and its later display-recovery path.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (mutant M2); published in Optional test improvement

leads.summary: The revised focus test passes if the actual focus operation is removed
leads.consequence: The tests recognize the request property and handler by grep but never test forcePasswordFocus's effect. Replacing passwordInput.forceActiveFocus() with a no-op preserves all assertions while the original keyboard-focus failure returns. Add a test of focus effect or an assertion of the method body, preferably the former.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus M5-style gap; published via the empty-handler mutant

leads.summary: Qt's password mask does not reveal the actual password when a mask glyph is unavailable (previously reported F7)
leads.consequence: The ASCII-mask change may improve glyph availability, but both explanatory claims about Qt exposing plaintext are false. At Qt 6.11.2 displayText fills with passwordCharacter independent of font coverage. This corroborates F7; it is not a new password disclosure finding.

leads.summary: lock-auth-failure-test still needs TMPDIR supplied by its caller (previously reported F8)
leads.consequence: With ordinary set -u and no exported TMPDIR, the test exits 1 after its first assertion rather than checking the password failure branch. The second changed test lock-focus-after-lid-test.sh now initializes and cleans TMPDIR at lines 7-8. Use a local mktemp -d/trap in lock-auth-failure-test.sh as well.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F8 half fixed)

flags.claim: Give EOF its own exit status in consume_sleep_events. Then either back off before retrying, or exit and let systemd's restart pacing handle it.
flags.why: A distinct status from consume_sleep_events alone changes nothing. The --inhibited) and --wait-resume) branches always 'exit 0' (bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor:114-121), and the main loop ignores run_child's return (138-153). My suggestion was to give EOF its own exit status in --inhibited / --wait-resume; the draft dropped the part about passing it through.

flags.claim: ...leaves the internal panel off for about 10 s and shows a false "still unlocked" alert.
flags.why: When the notification fires, no compositor lock is held (Service.qml:99-104). The session is still unlocked at that moment, so 'false' is too strong. The alert becomes out of date moments later, when the panel returns and the pending request locks. In the mock the notification is at 9986 ms and eDP-1 at 9994 ms. followup-1.md calls the message literally true at that moment.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12245#issuecomment-5835677295), checked at head `01dbad1`. Two earlier findings are resolved, the others still apply, and two new issues are described below.

**Verified:** both fixes described in the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12245#issuecomment-5841757745) resolve the earlier findings. Password submit now reaches PAM, and a lock requested while only `FALLBACK` exists now stays pending until a real display appears.

The other earlier findings are in code these commits did not change, and they still apply, except that one of the two `TMPDIR` tests is now fixed. One of them (echo-on PAM prompts) can now actually be reached. This round also found a sleep-monitor retry loop with no delay, and a problem that appears if open PR #9429 is merged as well.

| Earlier finding | At `01dbad1` |
|---|---|
| Password submits throw before PAM starts | **Resolved** |
| Lock with no physical display dropped after 15 s | **Resolved** |
| Sleep monitor can miss the resume signal (and the SIGTERM-between-children note) | Still present (file unchanged) |
| Relock rate limit leaves the desktop open | Still present (code unchanged) |
| Echo-on PAM prompts leave authentication stuck | Still present, and now reachable because submit reaches PAM |
| Lock-failure propagation has no effect | Still present (file unchanged) |
| Mask comment claims a plaintext fallback | Still present (comment and test unchanged) |
| Tests and `TMPDIR` | Half fixed: `lock-focus-after-lid-test.sh` fixed, `lock-auth-failure-test.sh` unchanged |
| Earlier **Verified** list | Still holds (code unchanged; the bash tests still pass) |

### Resolved: password focus and submit

**Verified:** `forceLockPasswordFocus()` now only increments `passwordFocusRequest`. Each surface's `LockView` binds that counter from `root` and calls its own `forcePasswordFocus()` when it changes. `id: lockView` is gone, and no code refers to it any more. This works because Quickshell 0.3.1 creates each surface in `Service`'s context, so bindings inside the component can read `root.*`, while ids declared inside the component stay private.

A non-GUI Qt 6.11.2 analog, which copies the relevant functions and bindings from each revision:

| | Prior head `2c1db6d` | Head `01dbad1` |
|---|---|---|
| Submit | `ReferenceError: lockView is not defined`, PAM start count 0 | no error, PAM start count 1 |
| Focus calls per surface (two surfaces) | no further calls (same `ReferenceError`) | +1 on each surface after submit (wake) and after a screen change |
| Surface created later | focused once on creation (pre-existing `Component.onCompleted`) | same, other surfaces unchanged |

`Qt.callLater` removes duplicates per object and method, so each surface gets its own call. A negative control without the new handler showed no extra focus calls. Whether Hyprland gives keyboard focus to the right lock surface after a lid-open resume (#7811) was not tested.

### Resolved: lock requested with only `FALLBACK`

**Verified:** `clearStalledLockRequest()` now keeps the request when `!hasRealScreen()`. It resets only the acquire flags and re-arms the timeout. It no longer clears `lockRequested` or calls `runWake()`. The same analog with a mocked screen list and a mocked compositor grant, on each revision (only `FALLBACK` present, a `lock()` call at 20 s, a physical display added at 40 s):

```text
prior head: 15 s lock-failed: acquire-timeout; the 20 s request is dropped again at 35 s → display added at 40 s: stays unlocked
head:       15 s, 35 s lock-pending: waiting-for-screen (request kept) → display added at 40 s: locked, secure=true
```

With real screens present, behaviour is unchanged: the new branch runs only when there is no real screen.

A property of this design, not a new defect: while only `FALLBACK` exists, no compositor lock is held, while `isLocked()` returns `"true"`. That is the "keep pending" option the earlier review suggested. `lock status` still shows `sessionLocked: false` and `realScreens: 0`.

**Optional:** each 15 s cycle logs `lock-pending: waiting-for-screen`. That event also resets the de-duplication in `requestSessionLock()`, so `lock-pending: no-real-screen` is logged again on the next 100 ms tick. That is about 480 lines per hour while a lock waits with no display connected. Reusing `lock-pending: no-real-screen`, or skipping the log when the request is already pending, would avoid it.

**Optional documentation note:** the comment at `Service.qml:68` and the test message in `lock-focus-after-lid-test.sh` still call `FALLBACK` a Quickshell placeholder, while the new comment at `Service.qml:197` calls it Hyprland's, which matches the earlier review's reading of Hyprland source.

### New: sleep monitor retries without delay when `dbus-monitor` fails

This code is in `bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor`, which the new commits did not touch. It was not covered in the earlier review. When `dbus-monitor` exits at once (for example, when the system bus is unavailable or the monitor keeps dying), `consume_sleep_events` returns 0 on EOF, the same status as a real event. Both child modes end in `exit 0`, and the main loop has no delay and no exit on failure. The loop therefore starts again immediately. Because the main process never exits, the unit's `Restart=always` / `RestartSec=2` never applies.

| Mocked run of the real script, 5 s | Merge-base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `dbus-monitor` exits 1, logind answers | script exits after 5 ms; the unit's `RestartSec=2` then paces restarts (not run) | 657 `dbus-monitor`, 656 `systemd-inhibit`, 1312 `busctl` launches; about 5.2 s of CPU in total |
| All three commands fail | script exits 1 | 619 / 619 / 1239 launches; similar CPU |

**Impact:** While the failure lasts, roughly one core is busy, and each failed child writes to the journal. With a working logind, the loop also takes and drops a delay inhibitor on every pass. Neither version protects suspend during this failure: the difference is pacing. Only the mocked commands were run, not a real bus failure.

**Suggested change:** Give EOF its own exit status in `consume_sleep_events`, and pass it through the `--inhibited` and `--wait-resume` exits (which now always exit 0). The main loop can then back off before retrying, or exit and let systemd's restart pacing handle it.

### New: interaction with open PR #9429

On its own, this PR does not have this delay. [#9429](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/9429) changes `omarchy-system-lock` to wait up to 10 s for `secure`. If `secure` is not reached, it shows a critical "Screen did not lock" notification and exits 1. The two PRs do not conflict textually. In this PR, `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell` calls `omarchy-system-secure-if-closed-undocked` (and through it `omarchy-system-lock`) synchronously, before `enable_internal`. With only `FALLBACK` present, this PR does not report `secure` until a real screen exists. So with both PRs merged, the lock waits for a screen, while re-enabling the panel waits for the lock to finish.

```text
undock while lid closed, only FALLBACK:
  this PR alone: eDP-1 re-enabled after about 40 ms
  with #9429:    10 s wait → critical notification → eDP-1 re-enabled after about 10 s
lid close with internal panel disabled (a transient state: the panel is disabled only while docked):
  this PR alone: eDP-1 re-enabled after about 60 ms
  with #9429:    two waits in a row, two notifications, eDP-1 re-enabled after about 20 s
```

These times come from mocked runs of this PR's real scripts, with `hyprctl`, `busctl`, notifications and the shell's lock IPC modelled. Nothing ran against a real compositor, logind or suspend.

**Impact:** If both are merged, an undock with the lid closed leaves the internal panel off for about 10 s and shows a critical "still unlocked" alert, although the lock completes once the panel returns. A suspend during that wait may go ahead without a secure lock: in a mocked run with a 4 s budget, `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` gave up with "Screen did not lock before suspend", while this PR alone exited 0. That logind re-checks a closed lid and suspends after undock comes from systemd source, and a real suspend was not tested.

**Suggested change:** If both land, either request the lock without waiting in `omarchy-system-secure-if-closed-undocked`, or have #9429 treat `requested` with `realScreens == 0` as pending. The `lock status` output already reports `realScreens`.

**Optional test improvement:** The new assertion in `lock-acquire-timeout-test.sh` still passes when the new branch sets `lockRequested = false`, which brings back the dropped lock. Its greedy `[\s\S]*` also matches the `lockAcquireTimeoutTimer.restart()` in `lock()`. `lock-focus-after-lid-test.sh` still passes with an empty `onPasswordFocusRequestChanged` body. Anchoring the regex to the `if (!hasRealScreen())` block and checking that it does not clear `lockRequested` would catch the first of these.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of head `01dbad100b65379f85e1667a8e54da5d034330dd` against the earlier reviewed head `2c1db6d`, with dependency source read at Quickshell 0.3.1, Qt 6.11.2 and systemd v261, and the open PR #9429 at `3fa17d4`. Sandboxed command-only runs: non-GUI Qt analogs of the focus and pending-lock paths for both heads, all 12 PR test files on both heads (with and without `TMPDIR`), code mutants checked against the two edited tests, and mocked runs of the sleep monitor and the clamshell and lock scripts. Not tested on a live desktop, lock screen, compositor, PAM stack, logind or real suspend.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review with targeted follow-up questions and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
